subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Electron transfer
hotspots.description: Sodium's lone outer electron travels across to chlorine. This full transfer — not a share — is what makes the bond ionic.
hotspots.positionHint: The curved glowing path between the two atoms, with a small dot traveling along it when the layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the electron moving from sodium to chlorine.

hotspots.label: Attracting ions
hotspots.description: After the transfer, sodium is positive (Na⁺) and chlorine is negative (Cl⁻). Opposite charges pull the ions together — that pull is the ionic bond.
hotspots.positionHint: The space between the two atoms, where a + and − pair appears when the transfer layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the positive and negative ions being pulled together.

hotspots.label: Salt crystal lattice
hotspots.description: The repeating cube of alternating violet (Na⁺) and green (Cl⁻) ions below is a slice of the salt crystal lattice.
hotspots.positionHint: The grid of alternating colored cubes beneath the atoms, visible when the lattice layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the repeating crystal structure that millions of ions form.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A sodium atom and a chlorine atom float side by side, large in frame, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Sodium is a soft muted violet sphere, chlorine a soft muted green sphere, each with a thin shell ring. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the traveling transfer electron (amber / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Sodium sphere: soft muted violet matte, roughness ~0.5. Chlorine sphere: soft muted green matte, roughness ~0.5. Shell rings: thin translucent hairline circles. Lattice cells: small matte cubes alternating the violet and green, roughness ~0.6. Transfer dot: small saturated amber. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a sodium atom and a chlorine atom forming an ionic bond, built to be read as 'transfer an electron, make opposite charges, lock together as salt.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: two atoms side by side — LEFT sodium (sphere radius ~0.55, soft muted violet) and RIGHT chlorine (sphere radius ~0.5, soft muted green), centers separated by ~1.6. Each has a thin translucent hairline shell ring. Sodium's ring carries ONE small teal electron dot; chlorine's ring carries SEVEN small dots (one spot clearly empty).

2) TRANSFER (toggleable layer): a curved dashed path arcs from sodium's lone electron to chlorine's empty spot; a small saturated amber dot animates along the path (app-driven). After arrival, a soft + appears over sodium and a soft − over chlorine (app-drawn UI glyphs, not mesh text), and the two atoms ease slightly closer.

3) LATTICE (toggleable layer): below the atom pair, a small 3×3×3 cube grid of alternating violet and green cells (each cell a small cube, edge ~0.18, muted) — a visible slice of the salt crystal lattice.

Camera: framed so the two atoms are large and centered with the lattice appearing below; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: SodiumAtom, ChlorineAtom, ShellRing_Na, ShellRing_Cl, SodiumElectron, ChlorineElectrons_07, TransferPath, TransferDot, LatticeCells, LatticeCell_Na, LatticeCell_Cl. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
